title: Hunt.io: exposed server of a Russian-speaking operator holds US bank, IRS and federal-benefit logins stolen from infected PCs
summary: Hunt.io found an open directory on a server of an unnamed Russian-speaking operator holding 1,692 files (about 1.11 GB). It reports at least 57 victims with a US bank or government login and at least 46 with a federal benefits or identity account, from 603 implant IDs. Hunt.io says no bank or agency was breached; the counts are floors and measure exposure.
plain: Researchers found a criminal's server full of logins stolen from infected home and work PCs, including bank and government accounts. The banks themselves were not hacked.
exec: Stolen session cookies and password vaults can bypass MFA at staff and customer accounts; infostealer exposure is an account-takeover risk.
action: Hunt for the published infrastructure, rotate passwords and revoke sessions on any PC with infostealer signs, and check for unexpected Level.io or ScreenConnect installs.

key_findings: Open directory with 1,692 files, about 1.11 GB; 603 unique implant IDs and 469 hostnames in the 12 Oct to 8 Nov 2026 campaign window.
At least 57 victims with a US bank or government login; at least 46 with a federal benefits or identity account; Hunt.io calls both floors.
Russian-speaking is inferred from Russian text in scripts and logs; no named threat group.
Hunt.io states no bank or agency was breached.
recommendations: Use the published infrastructure indicators for hunting; rotate credentials and revoke sessions on affected PCs.

validation.note: Original Hunt.io post read; GBHackers report read and consistent. The findings are the vendor's own.

review.note: Compared 1,692 files/1.11 GB, 57 and 46 floors, 603 IDs, 12 Oct-8 Nov window, no-breach statement against Hunt.io post and GBHackers
